title: Fill parameterized cones from their universal initial or final vertices
statement:
Use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the relative diagrams and join cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a quasicategory and $P\subseteq B$ a simplicial subset. Then $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal E)$ are quasicategories, and restriction
$$r:\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal E)$$
is an isofibration: it has the right lifting property for inner horns, and every equivalence in the target with source $r(x)$ lifts to an equivalence with source $x$.
Suppose additionally that $P$ contains every vertex of $B$, and let $K$ be any simplicial set. Given a map
$$v:(B\times K)\amalg_{P\times K}(P\times K^{\triangleright})\to\mathcal E,$$
assume that, for every simplex $\sigma:\Delta^d\to B$ not belonging to $P$, the specified cocone $v|_{\{\sigma(0)\}\times K^{\triangleright}}$ is a colimit. There exists an extension $\bar v:B\times K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$. Every such extension, regarded as $K^{\triangleright}\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E)$, is an $r$-colimit diagram.
Dually, given a map on $(B\times K)\amalg_{P\times K}(P\times K^{\triangleleft})$, if its specified cone at $\sigma(d)$ is a limit for every simplex $\sigma:\Delta^d\to B$ outside $P$, it extends to $B\times K^{\triangleleft}$, and every extension is an $r$-limit diagram. All extensions agree exactly with the given maps on the indicated union. The simplicial sets and quasicategories are small in a fixed sufficiently large universe; no other colimits or limits in $\mathcal E$ are assumed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.1.8.7 with the base quasicategory equal to a point, Corollary 7.1.8.11 (relative-universality assertion), and their opposite duals. The structural restriction assertion is Corollary 4.4.5.3; the source explicitly states it is an isofibration of infinity categories. Read also Proposition 7.1.8.10. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online source, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Use the internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the explicit joins and relative predicates of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to $P\hookrightarrow B$: its restriction clause gives the two functor quasicategories and the isofibration $r$, including equivalence lifting. This part does not require the vertex hypothesis.

Put $X=\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal E)$, $Y=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ and let $q:X\to Y$ be restriction. It is an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Curry $v$ to compatible maps $g:P\to X$ and $f:B\to Y$. For a simplex $\sigma$ outside $P$, $g(\sigma(0))$ is the supplied ordinary colimit cocone. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocone-restriction-initial], restriction induces a weak equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_X(g(\sigma(0)),t)\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(qg(\sigma(0)),qt)$ for every $t\in X$, including arbitrary boundary diagrams $qt$. This is exactly $q$-initiality as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary].

Here is the lifting construction we will use twice. Let $A\subseteq T$ contain every vertex, with compatible maps $a:A\to X$ and $b:T\to Y$, and suppose $a(\tau(0))$ is $q$-initial for every simplex $\tau$ outside $A$. Use the relative skeletal pushouts of [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], starting from $A$. At stage $d$ attach the nondegenerate $d$-simplices outside $A$; their boundaries were attached earlier. There are no $0$-cells, since all vertices lie in $A$. For each attaching simplex the existing boundary map has initial vertex $a(\tau(0))$, so [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] gives a filler over its prescribed $Y$-simplex. Choose fillers for this small set of cells, glue by the attaching pushout, and continue by induction on $d$. The compatible maps on all stages induce a map on their colimit $T$; its restriction to $A$ and projection to $Y$ are the original maps, because both equalities hold at every stage. The dual construction uses $q$-final vertices $a(\tau(d))$ and the final-vertex boundary criterion.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.8.7 proof, explicit relative skeletal version of the extension argument

proof.text: Apply the construction of step 3 with $A=P$, $T=B$, and $(a,b)=(g,f)$ from step 2. Its hypotheses hold because the vertex condition is assumed and all required vertices were proved $q$-initial in step 2. It yields $h:B\to X$ with $h|_P=g$ and $qh=f$. By the formula for internal functor simplicial sets, uncurrying gives $\bar v:B\times K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$. These two equalities say exactly that it extends both parts of the prescribed pushout union.

source.place: Terminal-base extension, uncurrying the constructed lift

proof.text:
Fix any such extension $h$, not only the one constructed above. Form
$$Q:\operatorname{Fun}(B,X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(P,X)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(P,Y)}\operatorname{Fun}(B,Y).$$
It is an isofibration between quasicategories by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], applied to $q$ and $P\hookrightarrow B$. To test whether $h$ is $Q$-initial, the boundary criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] asks for lifts of $\partial\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,X)$ over a prescribed $\Delta^n$ in the target, with $n>0$ and initial vertex $h$. Uncurrying gives a map into $X$ on
$$S=(\partial\Delta^n\times B)\cup(\Delta^n\times P)\subseteq T=\Delta^n\times B$$
over a prescribed map $T\to Y$. The overlap equation is exactly the pullback equation in the target of $Q$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.8.10 proof, boundary lifting after replacing the original functor by cone restriction

proof.text: Every vertex of $T$ lies in $S$ because $n>0$. A simplex $(\alpha,\beta):\Delta^d\to\Delta^n\times B$ outside $S$ has $\alpha$ surjective on $[n]$ (otherwise it belongs to a boundary face) and $\beta$ not in $P$. Hence $\alpha(0)=0$. The specified map $S\to X$ at its initial vertex is therefore $h(\beta(0))=g(\beta(0))$, since $P$ contains all vertices. It is $q$-initial by step 2 applied to $\beta$. The skeletal construction of step 3, using [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] and [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary], fills $T$ over $Y$ while fixing $S$. Currying yields the required $Q$-boundary lift. The converse implication of the boundary criterion now proves that $h$ is $Q$-initial.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 7.1.8.10; use the union with the factor Delta^n times P

proof.text:
Currying exchanges $B$ and $K^{\triangleright}$ and also exchanges $P$ and $K$ in the lower corners. Degree by degree, $Q$ is thus the corner of $r$ along $K\hookrightarrow K^{\triangleright}$: its source becomes $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E))$ and its target becomes
$$\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal E))}\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal E)).$$
These identifications are induced by permuting product coordinates and commute with all simplicial operators. The relative-initial condition on mapping spaces is unchanged by these isomorphisms. Since $r$ is an isofibration, [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-initial-corner] converts step 6 into precisely the required $r$-colimit predicate for this arbitrary extension.

For the limit data set $X^-=\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleleft},\mathcal E)$, $Y=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ and $q^-:X^-\to Y$ the restriction isofibration from [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Curry the prescribed union to $g^-:P\to X^-$ and $f:B\to Y$. Fix a simplex $\sigma$ outside $P$ and let $u=g^-(\sigma(d))$, with apex $y$ and boundary $F$. Its coherent cone $\mu:\Delta_Ky\to F$ is limiting. The criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that $e_x:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(\Delta_Kx,F)$, $a\mapsto\mu\Delta_K(a)$, is a weak equivalence for every $x$. For any $t\in X^-$ with apex $x$, boundary $G$, and cone $\lambda$, [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] identifies restriction $\operatorname{Map}_{X^-}(t,u)\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(G,F)$ with projection from the homotopy pullback of $e_x$ along $b\mapsto b\lambda$. This projection is a weak equivalence: apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to replace $e_x:V\to W$ by $1_W:W\to W$ (the maps on the other factor and on $W$ are identities), then use [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] with the Kan fibration $1_W$ to compare the new path pullback with its strict pullback $\operatorname{Map}_Y(G,F)$. Both comparisons commute with projection, so two-out-of-three gives the claim. Consequently $u$ is $q^-$-final by the definition in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary]. The final-vertex construction in step 3, using [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], gives $h^-:B\to X^-$ over $f$ extending $g^-$; uncurrying gives an extension on $B\times K^{\triangleleft}$ fixing the entire given union.

source.place: Opposite dual, with the final-vertex boundary criterion

proof.text: For any limit extension $h^-$ form the corner $Q^-$ of $q^-$ along $P\hookrightarrow B$, an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Test the final-vertex boundary condition of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary]: a boundary of positive dimension $n$ whose last vertex is $h^-$ again uncurries to a map on $S=(\partial\Delta^n\times B)\cup(\Delta^n\times P)$ over $T=\Delta^n\times B$. For every missing simplex $(\alpha,\beta)$, $\alpha$ is surjective and $\beta$ is outside $P$; now $\alpha(d)=n$, so its final-vertex value is $h^-(\beta(d))=g^-(\beta(d))$, which is $q^-$-final by step 8. Apply the final-vertex skeletal construction using [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to fill $T$ fixing $S$. Thus every required boundary lifts and $h^-$ is $Q^-$-final. Permuting product coordinates identifies $Q^-$ with the corner of $r$ along $K\hookrightarrow K^{\triangleleft}$; [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-initial-corner] now makes this arbitrary extension an $r$-limit diagram.
